title: West Africa country profile evidence register
purpose: Track authoritative country-level agricultural survey sources before any values are admitted into GoOrganicAfrica calculator profiles.
publication_rules: Do not add a country to the active calculator dataset until its required commodity fields have been reviewed and validated.
Do not treat a country survey yield as a selling price or a complete farm budget.
Record commodity, production system, unit, geography, reference year, publication date, source URL, sampling uncertainty and any revision notice for every extracted value.
Use published aggregate tables unless the source explicitly authorizes the intended use of microdata.
Do not invent missing values. Leave unsupported fields for farmer entry or retain the clearly labelled Africa benchmark.
Do not change the calculator formula or the existing ten country profiles as part of this research package.

survey.extraction_status: The original October/November 2025 PDF is confirmed to be the old report: LISGIS now explicitly labels a corrected version available. The March 10 2026 erratum text corrects the Executive Summary and Key Findings; the later LISGIS portal notice says the LAAS-2024 report itself has a corrected version but does not expose its direct PDF URL in the accessible page text. Original Table 10 values therefore remain on hold. In the original PDF, rice 201,074 Mt / 139,707 harvested ha = 1.439 Mt/ha, not the reported 2.0; cassava 14,591 / 20,192 = 0.723, not 1.0; maize 2,937 / 3,438 = 0.854, not 1.5. The report body also labels its other-cost table as Table 35 and crop-labour wage table as Table 38, while the table-of-contents index lists these as Tables 38 and 41 respectively. Re-extract all figures and table references from the corrected PDF before using any data.

observation_caveats: All numeric values transcribed from the published October 2025 report are provisional and on hold pending identification of tables affected by the August 2026 LISGIS correction notice.

The report flags pepper planted area, rubber planted/harvested area, sweet-potato harvested area/production, eggplant harvested area/production and okra production as high-uncertainty indicators (CV > 33% or SE > 17.5%).
Cassava yield is timing-specific: only 28.3% of cassava households reported harvesting during the survey reference period, and the report warns that annual output may be understated.
A single national yield observation is not a low/expected/high calculator range.
Daily labour and other service-payment averages cannot be converted into per-hectare budgets without activity duration, worker counts and farm-system assumptions.

Arithmetic review found that the report's published yield values do not consistently reconcile with harvested quantity divided by harvested area (for example, rice: 201,074 Mt / 139,707 ha = about 1.439 Mt/ha, while the table reports 2.0 Mt/ha). Do not use the published yield column or the recalculated ratio until LISGIS confirms the correct yield denominator and resolves the August 2026 erratum.
The March 10 2026 LISGIS erratum identifies changes to the Executive Summary and Key Findings, not the crop-yield or labour tables transcribed here.

A separate August 2026 portal notice refers to selected corrected tables and indicators but does not identify the affected table numbers in the accessible notice; its relevance to LAAS-2024 remains to be confirmed.

An official corrected-report download is now identified on the LISGIS survey record. Re-extract Table 10 and the cost tables from that corrected report before treating earlier transcriptions as valid.

LISGIS's current survey record explicitly announces a corrected LAAS-2024 report; the older PDF previously used for transcription is labelled the old document on the portal. The corrected PDF must replace it as the source of record.
In the old report, rice, cassava and maize yield columns do not equal harvested quantity divided by harvested area. Recalculated ratios are diagnostics only and must not replace official yields.
The old report's body captions and table-of-contents numbering differ for other production costs and daily hired labour wages; re-identify by caption in the corrected PDF.
Do not include child labour wages or child labour cost assumptions in farm budgets.

additional_surveys.title: 2025 Sierra Leone National Crop Production Survey Report
additional_surveys.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS), Planning, Evaluation, Monitoring and Statistics Division (PEMSD)
additional_surveys.method: Crop-cutting yield measurements combined with GPS-measured cultivated area; stratified sampling by district and rice ecology. The report describes a 95% confidence level and 5% margin of error for the sampling design.
methodology_notes: Rice uses a district- and ecology-specific sampling frame and a target sample of approximately 6,300 rice-producing households.
Other major crops use the 2023 agricultural household listing frame and district-stratified sampling.
Onion observations were collected through targeted phone surveys of major private producers.
The report covers rice, cassava, maize, cocoa, sweet potato, groundnut and onion.
quality_notes: The national rice yield of 2.37 Mt/ha does not reconcile with 1,441,015 Mt divided by 661,016 ha (approximately 2.18 Mt/ha). Ask MAFS to clarify the yield denominator or corrected area before calculator use.
The report's district-level rice yields range from Moyamba at 1.53 Mt/ha to Kambia at 2.89 Mt/ha; these district observations should not automatically be treated as universal low/high scenarios.
The 2025 crop-cutting survey and 2024 household survey use different measurement methods; do not average their results without methodological reconciliation.
Reported point yields are not complete farm budgets or low/expected/high forecast bands.

The official April 2026 report describes the survey as covering the 2025/26 cropping season and uses crop-cutting, GPS area measurement and weighting. It states that rice grains were sun-dried to 14% moisture before yield measurement.

The report's national production and area imply 1,441,015 / 661,016 = approximately 2.180 Mt/ha, while its reported national average crop-cut yield is 2.37 Mt/ha. These may be different weighted estimands or denominator definitions; the report does not explain the reconciliation in the accessible text. Keep the 2.37 observation on hold pending a technical note from MAFS/PEMSD.

The report's district narrative says Port Loko produced approximately 184,916 Mt and Kambia 210,375 Mt, while describing Port Loko as the leading district and Kambia as second; the stated values reverse that ranking. Verify the district table or corrected report before using district production rankings.

Other-crop yields (cassava 12.54, maize 2.80, groundnut 2.33, cocoa 1.5 Mt/ha) are survey point estimates. The report summary does not provide all matching national area denominators; they are not automatically low/expected/high ranges.
additional_surveys.extraction_status: Official MAFS report PDF inspected directly. Survey method: stratified crop-specific sampling, rice ecology frame, crop cuts from 25/50 m² plots, rice dried to 14% moisture, GPS area and weighted aggregation. Official national rice yield 2.37 Mt/ha, production 1,441,015 Mt and cultivated area 661,016 ha. Their aggregate ratio is 2.180 Mt/ha, which is not reconciled in report text; district narrative also appears to reverse Port Loko/Kambia production ranking. Keep rice national and district observations on hold pending technical clarification. Other crop point yields may remain evidence leads but are not scenario ranges or cost/price data.
district_observation_caveats: Report narrative gives Port Loko rice production approximately 184,916 Mt and Kambia 210,375 Mt but says Port Loko is the leading district followed by Kambia. The stated figures contradict that ranking; verify against district table before quoting rankings.

system_observations.status: calculated production divided by cultivated area; diagnostic only; not a replacement for the report's weighted crop-cut yield
